settings.title: There are two distinct shuttle lines

settings.editor: The Springdale Line serves the gateway community; the Zion Canyon Line connects the visitor-center area with stops inside the canyon. Know which line matches your start and destination.

settings.editor: NPS states that the Zion shuttle is free and does not require a shuttle ticket, permit or reservation. Park entrance fees and hiking-specific permits are separate considerations.

settings.title: What visitors ask about shuttles & parking

tabs.tab_title: Do I need to buy a Zion shuttle ticket?
tabs.tab_content: No. NPS says the shuttle system is free to ride and requires no ticket or reservation.

tabs.tab_title: Can I drive my own car to the Narrows trailhead?
tabs.tab_content: During shuttle season, personal vehicle access on the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive is restricted. The Riverside Walk approach is reached from Temple of Sinawava.

tabs.tab_title: How long does the shuttle take?
tabs.tab_content: NPS estimates roughly 45 minutes one way for the full Zion Canyon Line. Exact service and waits vary.

tabs.tab_title: Where should I park in Springdale?
tabs.tab_content: Use authorized marked parking and follow current municipality and NPS instructions. Do not treat the town as unlimited free overflow parking.
